artists.biography:
The Undertones are a punk rock/New Wave band formed in Derry, Northern Ireland, in 1975. From 1975 to 1983, the Undertones consisted of Feargal Sharkey (vocals), John O'Neill (rhythm guitar, vocals), Damian O'Neill (lead guitar, vocals), Michael Bradley (bass, vocals) and Billy Doherty (drums). Although much of the earlier Undertones material drew influence from punk rock and new wave, the Undertones also incorporated elements of rock, glam rock and post-punk into material released after 1979, before citing soul and Motown as the influence for the material released on their final album. The Undertones released thirteen singles and four studio albums between 1978 and 1983 before Sharkey announced his intention to leave the band in May 1983, citing musical differences as the reason for the break up.
In 1999, the Undertones reformed, replacing lead singer Feargal Sharkey with Paul McLoone.

perplexity.description:
Released in 2020, West Bank Songs 1978–1983 (A Best Of) is a comprehensive retrospective of The Undertones, one of Northern Ireland’s most influential punk and new wave bands. The album compiles 42 tracks spanning their most vital years, capturing their signature blend of energetic rock, melodic pop-punk, and sharp, witty lyrics. Drawing from their early Sire Records releases—including their self-titled debut (1979) and Hypnotized (1980)—the collection highlights the band’s knack for combining Buzzcocks-like ferocity with the playful, juvenile spirit of the Ramones, all anchored by Feargal Sharkey’s distinctive vocals.

Musically, the album showcases The Undertones’ evolution from raw, guitar-driven punk to more polished, melodic pop-rock, with standout tracks like “Teenage Kicks,” “Wednesday Week,” and “Here Comes The Summer” exemplifying their knack for infectious hooks and relatable themes of adolescence and romance. The compilation also includes rarities and B-sides, offering a fuller picture of their creative output before Sharkey’s departure in 1983. Released by BMG and Salvo, West Bank Songs is widely regarded as an essential collection for fans and newcomers alike, praised for its breadth and the enduring quality of the band’s songwriting. Critics have noted that the album reaffirms The Undertones’ status as one of the most original and enduring acts of the late 1970s and early 1980s UK rock scene.
